title: Mip-NeRF: A Multiscale Representation for Anti-Aliasing Neural Radiance Fields
layout_note: Two lettered panels, (a) the prior approach and (b) the proposed one; (b) is itself two steps joined by a short arrow labelled with the approximating distribution, so the figure reads prior | ours-step-1 -> ours-step-2.
grouping: No frames or tints; panels are separated by whitespace and named underneath with a letter and the method name. The same camera-plus-pixel-grid motif opens each step so the panels align as variants of one scene.
shapes_depth: A camera is a small open triangle at the bottom left of each panel; the image is a tilted 3x3 pixel grid outlined in black. In (a) a single black ray with an arrowhead passes through the grid, with purple sample dots along it and a curved arrow from one dot up to the encoding symbol. In (b) the pixel is a red-outlined ellipse, the ray becomes a translucent purple cone cut into frustum segments (t0, t1), and in the last step the segment becomes a stack of soft purple Gaussian blobs inside a dashed cone outline with a curved arrow to the expected-encoding symbol. Line art only, no photos.
proposed_highlight: Colour is reserved for the new idea: the prior ray is black with small dots, while the proposed cone and its Gaussian approximation are the only filled, saturated (purple, red) shapes.
lesson: Contrast ray-based and cone-based sampling with the same camera-and-pixel-grid motif in each panel: a black line with point samples versus a translucent purple cone cut into frustum segments, then the same segment as stacked Gaussian blobs.
notes: venue ICCV from Semantic Scholar (venue_source: semantic-scholar); year = arXiv preprint year (2103.13415), the same as the ICCV year. Pure vector line art. Annotation note (2026-11-15): Concept teaser comparing sampling (ray vs cone), not a full method pipeline.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

core.what: NeRF (a, left) and Mip-NeRF (b, right) drawn side by side from the same camera glyph and tilted pixel grid: a single ray with point samples against a cone cut into a conical frustum, ours last

relations.form: both panels reuse the identical camera and 3 x 3 pixel grid; NeRF draws a black ray o + td with purple sample dots and gamma(x) lifted from one point, Mip-NeRF replaces it with a translucent purple cone over a red pixel footprint
the Mip-NeRF cone is cut into a frustum segment between t0 and t1 with the pixel radius r-dot marked on the footprint, the operation drawn on the ray geometry itself
within b) an arrow labelled N leads right from the frustum to the same scene where the frustum is replaced by stacked purple Gaussian blobs, lifted by a curved arrow to E[gamma(x)]

channels.colour: purple = the sampled volume (sample points in NeRF, cone and Gaussians in Mip-NeRF); red = the pixel's footprint; black = geometry (camera, grid, ray)
channels.shape: camera triangle, tilted grid = image plane; line = ray; cone/frustum = conical sample volume; ellipsoids = Gaussians
channels.line: solid = ray and cone edges; dashed = the faded continuation of the cone; curved arrows = encoding of a sample
channels.frame: no frames; panels separated by whitespace and captions

quality.strengths: the difference between point sampling and cone sampling is pure geometry on a shared scene - same camera, same grid, ray vs cone - so it reads with labels covered; the representation that is encoded (a point, then a Gaussian) is drawn at the spot it comes from with its encoding label above; one accent colour marks what changed
quality.weaknesses: r-dot, t0 and t1 are small italic labels sitting inside or under the translucent cone and are hard to read; purple marks both NeRF's sample points and Mip-NeRF's volumes, which is consistent in meaning but makes the NeRF sample dots faint

insights.structure: Two captioned sub-figures side by side, 'a) NeRF' at left and 'b) Mip-NeRF' at right, each built from the same camera glyph and tilted pixel grid; the Mip-NeRF part is two steps joined by an arrow labelled N.
insights.data: Rays are black lines with point samples, the cone is a translucent purple solid cut into frustum segments between t0 and t1, and the frustum is then shown as stacked purple Gaussian blobs; the encoding is written as gamma(x) versus E[gamma(x)].
insights.emphasis: The only colour is purple on the Mip-NeRF cone and Gaussians plus a red pixel footprint, against a black-line NeRF panel.
insights.flow: Left to right: ray to cone to Gaussians, with curved arrows lifting each sample up to its encoding label.
insights.avoid: Small italic labels (r-dot, t0, t1) sit inside the translucent cone and are hard to read.

arrangement.units: unframed side-by-side sub-figures with letter captions beneath, the same camera-and-grid motif in each
arrangement.inputs_as: camera glyph and pixel grid drawn in perspective
arrangement.shared: the same camera and pixel-grid motif repeated in each panel
